main_text.p: Maledicta est humus propter te).i. propter inobedientiam tuā. Explicatur pœna talionis, terrā rebellē fore Adamo, qui se Deo rebellem præstitisset. In dolore comedes eam) id est, quicquid ex ea natum fuerit.

Omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ) Explicat ordine partes maledictionis. Complectitur hæc sententia Dei, molestias & labores, dolores varij generis, infirmitates, morbos, fenium, & id genus mala, quæ opponuntur voluptati Edenis. Sed tolerabilem reddere debet hanc calamitatem, partim æqua sententia Dei in peccatum pronunciata, partim futuri seculi, quam expectamus, gloria & integritas, quæ his malis succedet, veluti Dominus his verbis promittit, Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolationem accipient.
Et spina atque tribulū)ꝓ fructiferis arboribꝰ.

Faciet crescere tibi: & manducabis herbas agri) Huc referuntur olera & legumina, pi-sum, fabæ, milium, far, triticum, hordeum. Cum hac sententia dei, voluptuariorum luxus pugnat, ut quæ nos ad frugalitatem inui-tet, & curam de lautiore victu eximat.

In fudore vultus tui vescéris pane) latissi-mé patet is fudor & labor. Non.n.unum mu-neris genus viro imponitur. Nullum autem munus caret suo fudore & molestia, quæ præbeatur ijs qui illo utuntur. Facessant igitur hic ociosi ventres, aduersus quos Apostolus, 2.Thef.3. Qui non laborat, non manducet.

page.notes: Page number read as "31" from a worn top-right numeral; treat as doubtful. The printed Greek-looking running head is set in capitals with V for U, normalised to NUPTIALES. The word in "maledictionis" has a worn letter pair after "maled", read as "ct"; uncertain. "Thef" in the scripture reference is printed as such and kept. The line break at "quæ prae-beatur" shows no visible hyphen, so the word is written whole. The first paragraph starts with a capital and no visible indent, so it is not marked as a continuation. The inline glosses in parentheses are part of the running text and are not marginal notes.
